title: autotune: default batching/caching heuristics + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Asha Kapoor
description: Motivation: reduce per-token unit cost and make cost-optimization defaults safe for most workloads by shipping autotuned defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching, add curated quantization profiles for common model families, and provide a unit-economics CLI/reporting tool so SREs and platform engineers can see expected cost-latency tradeoffs. This PR implements three coordinated pieces: 1) autotune defaults - runtime heuristics that pick default max_batch_size, batch_wait_ms, and proactive prefix caching policies based on historical latency/sequence distributions and customer tier; 2) quantization profiles - a small catalog of validated quantization configs (int8, nf4-qlo) per model-family with compatibility gating and graceful fallback; 3) unit-econ tooling - a new CLI subcommand (redwood ctl unit-econ) and backend endpoint that estimates per-route token cost, expected latency p95 under a selected profile, and cost delta vs current configuration. The description below summarizes scope, migration, testing, and rollout plan. Scope: serving/runtime - autotune heuristics, config schema and migration; serving/quant - profile registry, validation hooks and compatibility matrix; console + backend - unit-econ API, UI telemetry events, and a CLI wrapper; docs/examples - quickstart for tuning profiles and interpreting unit-econ reports. Migration: runtime reads new defaults from autotune_config v2; existing explicit customer configs are preserved. Quant profiles are opt-in by default for private/dedicated customers and auto-suggested for hosted routes. When a profile is unsupported on current hardware we fall back to nearest supported profile and surface a warning in the unit-econ output. Testing: added unit and integration tests covering policy selection, fallback behavior, and end-to-end unit-econ accuracy using synthetic traffic traces. Benchmarks: internal benchmark shows 12-28% token cost reduction on average depending on workload mix, with <5% p95 latency increase for tail-sensitive routes when conservative flags are enabled. Rollout plan: feature-flag gated rollout: 1) internal dogfood on staging (2 days), 2) gradual rollout to low-traffic customers (1 week), 3) enable auto-suggestions in console for all hosted customers (2 weeks) with opt-out. Related: ENG-7834 (autotune heuristics), ENG-7901 (quant profiles registry), PM-402 (unit-econ product spec).

release_notes: Added autotuned defaults for batching and prefix caching, a curated set of quantization profiles with compatibility checks, and a unit-economics estimator CLI + UI. Rollout is feature-flag gated; customers can opt out. Expected cost reductions: ~12-28% depending on workload. See docs/optimize/unit-econ.md for usage.
notes_for_soc: No customer data is surfaced by default; unit-econ estimator uses aggregated/anonymous histograms for hosted customers. Private customers with air-gapped install must opt-in to use profile suggestions. All profile applications are logged for audit and can be disabled via policy.
